_what: Every numeric value the DESIGN publishes, with the inputs that produce it. The test suite recomputes all of them from src/core and compares. If any one of these moves, the physics core has changed and the change is intentional or it is a defect; there is no third option.
_provenance: The coordinates in appendixB and workedPairs are the ones the design author used. They were recovered by solving for the coordinate that reproduces the design's own published distances, and they reproduce every one of them exactly. See coordinateNote on the Tokyo row.
_precision: Tolerances are the precision the design states, not the precision a double can hold. km values are published as integers except where a decimal is printed; ms values to 2 decimals except the per-1000-km constant, which is published to 4.

appendixB._what: DESIGN 4 C2 and Appendix B. Distances, floors, measured round trips, the access baseline, route surpluses and route ratios, all recomputed from the coordinates and the measured values below.

rows.note: Under 500 km, so no ratio is rendered. The expected ratio is asserted on the arithmetic only, to prove the baseline endpoint lands at exactly 1.00x by construction.

rows.coordinateNote: This is NOT the coordinate the shipped endpoint table uses. The design author used 35.6762, 139.6503 for Tokyo; the shipped table uses the Wikidata value 35.6894, 139.6917 (Q1490), because every shipped coordinate has to carry a citation a reader can re-pull. The two points are 4.017 km apart. From the Appendix B observer that is a distance difference of 3.079 km (10943.961 against 10947.041) and a floor difference of 0.0302 ms, which is three hundredths of a millisecond on a number this product renders in whole milliseconds. It is far below the uncertainty that actually governs here, namely that the coordinate is a city centre and not a building. All three figures are asserted explicitly in test/endpoints.test.js rather than left for someone to find.

workedPairs._what: DESIGN Appendix B, the two independently stated great circles and their floors.

positiveControl._what: THE TEST THAT MUST FAIL. DESIGN 7 requires a positive control, because a suite that has never been seen to fail proves only that it ran. This row states a distance that is deliberately wrong by 100 km. test/floor.test.js asserts that the SAME comparator used on every row above REJECTS this one. If this ever passes, the comparator has stopped comparing and every green result above is meaningless.
positiveControl.name: Mumbai with a deliberately wrong expected distance
